lines.japanese: 「いえ、僕も職業柄、あまり他人の趣味には口を出さないことにしてるんですけどね。でも、さすがにほら……見知った顔だと、こう……ねえ？」
lines.english: “Given my profession, I try not to comment too much on other people's tastes. But when it's a face I know, even I have to… well. You know?”

lines.japanese: 「いや口出していいよ。むしろ口出せよ。然るのち俺に全否定させろよ」
lines.english: “No, comment away. Actually, I want you to. Then let me shoot the whole thing down.”

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、最近よくアリスと遊んであげてるなーなんて思ってはいましたけど。ははっ、いや、はは……」
lines.english: “I had noticed you seemed to be playing with Alice rather often lately. Haha. No, ha…”

lines.japanese: 「あんさ。あの、今日たまたま見かけたワンショットをさも日常的な光景として扱うのとかやめてくんない。あと何ソレその、確信的に何かをつかんだような苦笑い」
lines.english: “Listen. Could you not take one random scene you happened to witness today and treat it like an everyday occurrence? And what's with that rueful laugh like you've finally grasped some terrible truth?”

lines.japanese: 俺たちはアリスとジャパニーズ指ゲームやら何やらで遊んでやったあと、真っ赤なランドセルを改札口まで見送った。
lines.english: After entertaining Alice with Japanese finger games and the like, we escorted the bright red schoolbag to the ticket gate.

lines.japanese: 次までにもっと強くなっておきなさい、というような意味の勝ち台詞を大人ふたりに残して、やつは満足げに帰っていった。
lines.english: She left the two adults with a victor's declaration to the effect that we should train harder before next time, then went home satisfied.

lines.japanese: なんだかんだ言ってもまだ子供、まだまだ純粋だ。三人の勝率が常に拮抗するよう、俺やプラチナがわざと勝ったり負けたりしてゲームバランスを調整していたことには気付いていない。
lines.english: Whatever else she might be, she was still a child and still innocent. She hadn't noticed that Platinum and I had deliberately won and lost to keep all three of our win rates roughly even.

lines.japanese: あの気位の高いお姫様が、世界はどこまで行ったって絶えず誰かしかの手の上なんだって思い知るのは、もう何年か先のことだろう。
lines.english: It would be several more years before that proud little princess learned that, no matter how far she went, the world still held her in the palm of someone else's hand.

lines.japanese: そして俺の心配がいまひとつ。
lines.english: Which left me with one more concern.

lines.japanese: 子供のうちからこんなハイレベルのイケメンふたりに相手してもらって、やつが将来ものすごい面食いに育ってしまったらどうしよう。
lines.english: What if being entertained by two such exceptionally handsome men while she was still a child left her with impossibly high standards for men when she grew up?

lines.japanese: 俺も罪な男だ。
lines.english: It was a crime to be this charming.

lines.japanese: 「フッ」
lines.english: “Heh.”

lines.japanese: 「あの、ドラさん……なぜ物思いに耽りながら笑ってるんですか……」
lines.english: “Um, Dora... Why are you smiling while lost in thought?”

lines.japanese: 「まァ、俺も罪な男だからな」
lines.english: “Well, being this charming is practically a crime.”

lines.japanese: 「そんな、まだ刑法には触れてないですよ！」
lines.english: “Come on, you haven't actually broken any laws yet!”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そういう意味の罪じゃなくてね」
lines.english: “That's not the kind of crime I meant.”

lines.japanese: そして俺は数分ほどかけて、自分の趣味が妖艶な色香の漂う女豹のような女であることを、こんこんと説く羽目になった。
lines.english: And so I was forced to spend several minutes patiently explaining that my type was a woman like a panther, dripping with sultry allure.

lines.japanese: 「なんだ、じゃあ、そういう女性と付きあえばいいじゃないですか」
lines.english: “Well, then why don't you date a woman like that?”

lines.japanese: 美形で金持ちで積極的という、いかにも選びとる側の人種らしい発想だった。俺は鼻毛をひっこ抜きながらそうですねと答えて、この話をめでたく打ちきった。
lines.english: It was exactly the kind of idea you'd expect from a handsome, wealthy, assertive member of the species accustomed to doing the choosing. I plucked out a nose hair, told him that was an excellent point, and brought the conversation to a happy end.

lines.japanese: 「でもドラさん、もし本当に切実なときは、血迷う前にまず相談してください」
lines.english: “Still, Dora, if things ever become truly desperate, please talk to me before you lose your head.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　なにが」
lines.english: “Huh? About what?”

lines.japanese: 「実は七個前の彼女が、いまソープに勤めてるんです。こちらの深刻な事情を説明すればきっと破格で──」
lines.english: “Actually, the girlfriend from seven relationships ago works at an erotic bathhouse now. If I explain your grave circumstances, I'm sure she'll give you an exceptional—”

lines.japanese: 「そうだ、鼻毛やるよ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. You can have my nose hair.”

lines.japanese: 俺はプラチナの高級スーツに親指をこすりつけた。
lines.english: I rubbed my thumb against Platinum's expensive suit.

lines.japanese: 「さて、丁度いい時間かな」
lines.english: “Well, this looks like the perfect time.”

lines.japanese: プラチナは左腕の袖をわずかに引いて、白金の腕時計に目を落とした。パルさんの値踏みによると、それはちょっとした軽自動車が買えるぐらいの値がする代物らしい。
lines.english: Platinum tugged back his left sleeve and glanced at his platinum watch. According to Paru's appraisal, it was worth about as much as a small car.

lines.japanese: はいはい。俺は上半身を後ろにひねって、財布をいためることなく駅ビルの時計を見上げた。
lines.english: Yeah, yeah. I twisted around and looked up at the station clock, which hadn't cost my wallet a thing.

lines.japanese: 「おや、ドラさんもこれからお仕事ですか」
lines.english: “Oh? Are you on your way to work too, Dora?”

lines.japanese: 「んー？　んー、仕事っつうか、まあバイトだけど」
lines.english: “Hmm? Well, work... It's just a temp job.”

lines.japanese: なぜか訂正する俺。
lines.english: For some reason, I corrected him.

lines.japanese: 寒空に白い劣等感を吐きちらしながら、俺は作業着と安全帽と軍手とふかふかタオル他の詰まったスポーツバッグを担ぎなおした。よっこいしょ。
lines.english: Scattering white clouds of inferiority into the cold air, I resettled the sports bag stuffed with my work clothes, hard hat, gloves, fluffy towel, and assorted other gear. Heave-ho.

lines.japanese: 「今日はどんなお仕事です？」
lines.english: “What kind of work are you doing today?”

lines.japanese: 「どんなって、まー、普通？　フツーにドカチン」
lines.english: “What kind? I dunno. Ordinary. Plain old construction work.”

lines.japanese: 「んー！　フツーに普通ができるなんて、そういうところドラさんは偉いですよねえー」
lines.english: “Ahh! You can live an ordinary life as though it were the easiest thing in the world. I really admire that about you, Dora.”

lines.japanese: 普通の難しさを味わってきた地方出身の元役者志望は、たっぷり感慨をこめたような白い息を吐いた。本当に感慨がこもっていたかは知らない。プラチナは感情を偽るプロフェッショナルだ。
lines.english: The former would-be actor from the provinces, who knew firsthand how hard it was to be ordinary, breathed out a white cloud that seemed weighted with emotion. Whether it truly was, I couldn’t say. Platinum was a professional at faking feelings.

lines.japanese: 俺はヘタクソな演技で普通が一番だよと返した。だけどやっぱり、素人が心にもないことを言うのは難しかった。俺はこちらばかり質問されるのが面倒になった。
lines.english: With some amateurish acting of my own, I told him ordinary was best. But an amateur had trouble saying things he didn't mean. I grew tired of being the only one answering questions.

lines.japanese: 「そっちは」
lines.english: “What about you?”

lines.japanese: 「はい？」
lines.english: “Yes?”

lines.japanese: 「いまからまた街頭立って、ひと仕事すんの」
lines.english: “Going back out on the street to drum up some business?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ。いえ、このあとは人と会う予定になってまして。先方の希望でもあるので、どこか静かに話せるバーでも……あはは、やだなあ違いますよ、仕事ですってば」
lines.english: “Yes. Well, no, I'm meeting someone after this. She requested it, so I thought we might find a quiet bar where we can talk... Ahaha, come on, it isn't like that. This is work.”

lines.japanese: 俺は何も言ってないのに、また例によって表情を読まれたみたいだ。やつはデート疑惑を否定して続ける。
lines.english: I hadn't said a word, but as usual he seemed to have read my face. He denied the unspoken accusation of a date and went on.

lines.japanese: 「おととい声かけた女の子から、すこし詳しい話が聞いてみたいっていう電話をもらったんです。ただほら、ファミレスやカフェだと、勧誘行為禁止って言って神経過敏になってるところ多いでしょう」
lines.english: “A girl I approached the day before yesterday called to say she wanted to hear more. But family restaurants and cafés tend to get nervous and ban solicitation, you know.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、そう言って酒を出す店へ連れこんで。はー、悪の道へ誘っちゃうんだ」
lines.english: “Ah, so you use that excuse to get her into a place that serves booze. Then lure her down the path of evil.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、ひどいなあ。ドラさんまで、悪だなんて言わないでくださいよ。僕がお世話になってる事務所は裏モノとか関わってないし、僕だって力技で言いくるめるような真似はしないんですから」
lines.english: “Come on, that’s cruel. Don’t you start calling it evil too, Dora. The agency I work with has nothing to do with illegal porn, and I don’t strong-arm anyone into saying yes.”

lines.japanese: キャッチやらホストやらＡＶのエキストラやらを経て現在ＡＶ女優のスカウトに至った男は、人好きのする健康的な笑顔でハキハキと語る。今日も王子様みたいな白い歯がまぶしい。
lines.english: After stints as a street tout, a host, and an adult-film extra, he had wound up scouting actresses for the industry. He delivered this speech with the open, wholesome smile that made people like him. His princely white teeth dazzled today as ever.

lines.japanese: 「まあ、路上で最初に声かけるときは、多少しつこくもしちゃいますけどね。でも最終的には、そんな強引なことはしないんです。本人の意思で決意を固めてもらわないと、結局あとでこっちが痛い目を見ますから」
lines.english: “I can be a little persistent when I first approach someone on the street. But in the end, I never force the issue. If she doesn’t make up her own mind, we’re the ones who get burned later.”

lines.japanese: 「本人の意思。はあ。じゃーなに、世の中には自分から進んで裸とか交尾とか見せたがる女がいっぱいいるって、そういうことなわけ」
lines.english: “Her own choice. Huh. So what, the world’s full of women who actually want strangers to see them naked or having sex? That what you’re saying?”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、そういう芸術肌の子もいるとは聞きますけど、僕は当たったことないですねえ。相応の対価を求めて踏みきるのが一般的だと思いますよ」
lines.english: “Hmm. I've heard there are artistic souls like that, but I've never met one. Usually, I think they take the plunge for the money.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、金」
lines.english: “Ah. Money.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ。そもそも僕の場合、そういう臭いを感じた子にしか声をかけませんし」
lines.english: “Exactly. I only approach girls when I catch that particular scent on them in the first place.”

lines.japanese: 「臭いねぇ……はん、とりあえず行くか」
lines.english: “A scent, huh... Hmph. Let's get moving.”

lines.japanese: いつまでも立ち話をしてたって仕方ない。俺たちは柳木原のいちばんでっかい交差点へ向かって歩きはじめた。
lines.english: There was no point standing around talking forever. We started toward the largest intersection in Yanagihara.

lines.japanese: アルバトロスの巨大な街頭ビジョンでは、ＯＬ姿に扮したグラビアアイドルが、消費者金融の手軽さと利便性を清々しく謳っていた。
lines.english: On the Albatross’s enormous street screen, a pinup model dressed like an office worker sang the praises of easy, convenient consumer loans.

lines.japanese: ２１世紀の繁華街では、破滅への入り口もＦカップねーちゃんの笑顔でデコレートされてる。まさしく現代の怪談。ご利用は計画的に。
lines.english: In a twenty-first-century entertainment district, even the entrance to ruin came decorated with the smile of an F-cup beauty. A modern ghost story if ever there was one. Borrow responsibly.

lines.japanese: 「たとえばいまから会う子は、全身ばっちりキメキメで歩いてたんですよ。こう、頭からつま先まで……ああ訂正。頭から膝のあたりまででした」
lines.english: “For example, the girl I'm meeting now was walking around dressed to perfection from head to toe. Everything, from the crown of her head down to... Ah, correction. Down to about the knees.”

lines.japanese: 「こまけーよ。んなディティールどーでもいいよ」
lines.english: “You’re splitting hairs. Who gives a shit about that detail?”

lines.japanese: 喋ることを生業とするプラチナは、強弱を付けた営業くさい口調で淀みなく語りあげる。
lines.english: Platinum, who made his living with words, delivered the story without a stumble in his emphatic, sales-pitch cadence.

lines.japanese: 「気合の入ってる子でした。クチュール風のウールコートも、モテかわ系のツインニットも、チャコールグレイのシガレットパンツも、シャンパンゴールドのトートバッグも、ぜんぶ流行りのブランドで固めてまして」
lines.english: “She was certainly committed. The couture-inspired wool coat, the sweet-and-pretty twin-knit set, the charcoal-gray cigarette pants, the champagne-gold tote bag—all of it from fashionable brands.”

lines.japanese: 「ところがこのお嬢さん、じっと目を凝らしてよくよく見れば、ブーツだけが微妙にフェイクの予感。さて、ここで問題です。彼女はいったいどんな女の子でしょう」
lines.english: “But when I narrowed my eyes and really studied her, the boots alone looked suspiciously fake. So, question time: what sort of girl was she?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　あ、いや、分かんね。見栄っ張り？」
lines.english: “Huh? Uh, I dunno. A show-off?”

lines.japanese: 「見栄っ張りでアンテナ高いけど、経済力が追いついてない」
lines.english: “A fashion-conscious show-off whose wallet can't keep up.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ……おまえ、エグいな。ひとをそういう偏見の目で見てんのかよ」
lines.english: “Damn... You’re ruthless. That’s really how you size people up? Through that kind of prejudice?”

lines.japanese: 「ねー？　まーったく、いつの間にこんな捻くれた大人に育っちゃったんでしょう。ぼかぁもう、田舎の両親に会わせる顔がなかですわ、ははははは」
lines.english: “Isn’t it awful? When did I grow into such a twisted adult? Why, I can’t hardly show my face to Ma and Pa back home no more. Hahahahaha.”

lines.japanese: やつにしては珍しくヘタな笑い方だった。
lines.english: For him, that was an unusually bad laugh.

lines.japanese: 「そういえばドラさん、結局この前は観に行かれたんですか？」
lines.english: “Speaking of which, Dora, did you end up going to see it the other day?”

lines.japanese: 信号待ちの雑踏に溶けこんで冬の寒さに足踏みしているとき、やつがふと思いだしたように言った。
lines.english: We had melted into the crowd waiting at the light and were stamping our feet against the winter cold when he spoke as though the thought had just returned.

lines.japanese: 「あ？　俺がなにを」
lines.english: “Huh? See what?”

lines.japanese: 「ほら、この前お会いしたとき、ハリュー・クロードのジェンベを気に掛けてたでしょう」
lines.english: “Remember? The last time we met, you were curious about Haryu Claude's djembe.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ、あーあー、あれか」
lines.english: “Oh. Oh, right. That.”

lines.japanese: 無愛想なカリスマドラマーが陰気なオーディエンスに贈る、ものものしいストリートライブ。最後には鋼の財布と呼ばれるこの俺が、なんと７成田ドルもの高評価を下したほどに熱いステージだった。
lines.english: A portentous street performance, offered by a surly, charismatic drummer to a dour audience. By the end, even I—the man they called the Iron Wallet—had rated that scorching set at a staggering seven Narita dollars.

lines.japanese: 「おー、行った行った。燃えた燃えた」
lines.english: “Yeah, I went. Got me fired up. Fired me right up.”

lines.japanese: つうか、そうだ、俺も聞こうと思ってたんだ。
lines.english: Actually, right. I'd meant to ask him too.

lines.japanese: 「なあ、あれ以来あの太鼓が聞こえてこねーんだけどさ。あのハリューとかいう太鼓のあんちゃん、しょっちゅう路上ライブやってるわけじゃないの」
lines.english: “Hey, I haven't heard those drums since. That Haryu guy—he doesn't play on the street all that often?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、はい、そうですね。僕も仕事柄ほぼ毎日柳木原に通ってますけど、そう何度もは耳にしてないかな」
lines.english: “No, I suppose not. My work brings me to Yanagihara almost every day, and I still haven’t heard him very often.”

lines.japanese: 「へー、マジで」
lines.english: “Huh. Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「はい。しかもアレなんですよ、例の三個前の彼女に聞いた話ですけど、あのハリューというひとは事前に告知のたぐいを一切出さないそうで」
lines.english: “Yes. And there's another thing. This is something I heard from the girlfriend three relationships ago, but apparently Haryu never gives any advance notice at all.”

lines.japanese: 「え、そうなの」
lines.english: “Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、それなのに場所も時間帯も一定しないしで、フォロワーのあいだじゃ、もっぱら神出鬼没で有名らしいです」
lines.english: “Yes. The place and time change too, so among his followers he's famous for appearing and disappearing without warning.”

lines.japanese: 「はぁー。すんげえ適当だな。つか、もはや聞いてもらう気ねーだろソレ」
lines.english: “Damn. That's amazingly half-assed. At that point he doesn't even want anyone to hear him.”

lines.japanese: 接客態度も最悪だったしな。まあ、愛想のなさに関しちゃ、俺もひとのことは言えないんだけど。
lines.english: His customer service had been abysmal too. Though when it came to being unfriendly, I wasn't one to talk.

lines.japanese: しかし長い信号だ。俺は頬の裏を撫でながら、対岸のビルを見上げた。交差点には街頭ビジョンの広告用ナレーションが、環境法で認められている範囲の柔らかい音量で降りそそいでいた。
lines.english: This light was taking forever. Rubbing the inside of my cheek, I looked up at the buildings across the road. Commercial narration from the street screens rained over the intersection at the gentle volume allowed by the noise ordinances.

lines.japanese: 「あれ……でも、こないだ俺が行ったときは、なんか専属グルーピーみたいのがいっぱい、ハリューの周りグル～取りかこんでたぞ。告知なしの突発イベントにしちゃ、あいつらよくあんなに集まれたな」
lines.english: “Wait... When I went the other day, a whole crowd of what looked like his personal groupies had him completely surrounded. They sure managed to turn up at the right time for an unannounced show.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、やっぱりいました？　ははっ、黒ずくめの“いかにも”な子たちでしょう？」
lines.english: “Oh, they were there after all? Haha. All in black, looking every inch the part?”

lines.japanese: 黒ずくめのいかにもなガキ共……たしかにその通りだ。俺は頷いた。
lines.english: Kids in black who looked every inch the part... Exactly right. I nodded.

lines.japanese: 「それＲ－ウィングです。ええと、サッカーで言うところのフーリガンみたいなものでしょうか……タチの悪い熱狂的な親衛隊なんです」
lines.english: “That's R-Wing. In soccer terms, I suppose they're like hooligans... an unpleasant, fanatical personal guard.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それ。Ｒ……」
lines.english: “Oh. That. R...”

lines.japanese: Ｒなんたら。聞き覚えがあった。
lines.english: R-something. I'd heard it before.

lines.japanese: そうだ、さっきの幽霊女が自分たちのことをそう呼んでいた。Ｒ－ウィング。
lines.english: Right. The ghost woman earlier had called her group that. R-Wing.

lines.japanese: 繋がった。やっぱりあの無駄にデカい三人組は、あの夜ガード下に集まっていたハリュー・クロード親衛隊の一員だったんだ。だからなんだって話。
lines.english: The pieces connected. So those three needlessly enormous freaks really had been members of Haryu Claude's guard beneath the tracks that night. Not that it meant anything.

lines.japanese: 「行きましょう」
lines.english: “Let's go.”

lines.japanese: 信号が青になって、俺たちは横断者でいっぱいのゼブラゾーンを渡りはじめた。
lines.english: The light turned green, and we joined the flood of pedestrians across the crosswalk.

lines.japanese: 「なあ、そんで何。なんであいつら、そんないつどこで始まるかも分かんねー太鼓ショウに、ちゃっかり都合よく集まってたわけ」
lines.english: “So what gives? How’d they all manage to turn up in the right place for a drum show nobody knew when or where would start?”

lines.japanese: 「はは、単純ですよ。彼らが日頃から、組織的に柳木原じゅうを巡回しているからです」
lines.english: “Haha. It's simple. They run coordinated patrols all over Yanagihara every day.”

lines.japanese: 「マジで？　うわ、暇人……」
lines.english: “Seriously? Damn, they have nothing to do...”

lines.japanese: 「まったくです。でもこれが意外なことに、呆れるほど統制のとれてる集団なんです」
lines.english: “Quite. But surprisingly, they're disciplined to an absurd degree.”

lines.japanese: 「たとえば、巡回中に誰かひとりでもジェンベの音をキャッチしようものなら、たちどころに仲間全員へ連絡が行きわたり、たちまち現場へどどどどどーって」
lines.english: “For instance, the moment even one patrol member catches the sound of a djembe, word goes out to every comrade at once, and they all go thundering straight to the scene.”

lines.japanese: 「一度たまたまその非常召集を目撃したことありますけど、すごかったですよ。あの格好の集団が全力疾走ですもん、みんな不気味がってました」
lines.english: “I happened to see one of those emergency call-ups once. It was quite a sight. A whole group in those outfits sprinting at full speed—everyone thought it was creepy.”

lines.japanese: げ、あいつら、日常的にあのライブ仕様な服でうろつき回ってんのか。勇気あんな。
lines.english: Ugh. They wandered around dressed for the concert every day? That took nerve.

lines.japanese: 「つうか、なんかそれ変則オリエンテーションみたいだな。むしろバラエティ番組みたいで楽しそうじゃん」
lines.english: “That sounds like some weird-ass orientation exercise. Actually, it sounds more like a game show. Kinda fun.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、でしょうね。楽しいんだと思いますよ、当人たちは。要は、気の合う仲間と、街じゅう使って鬼ごっこですもん」
lines.english: “Haha. I imagine it is, for them. Essentially, they're playing tag with like-minded friends across the entire city.”

lines.japanese: プラチナは例の爽やかスマイルを崩すことなく続けた。
lines.english: Platinum went on, his usual bright, wholesome smile never faltering.

lines.japanese: 「でも、目立つ格好の若者が固まって集まれば、それだけで近寄りがたい雰囲気になるじゃないですか。それで周りが目を逸らして避けていくものだから、どんどん気が大きくなってしまったんでしょう──」
lines.english: “But when young people in conspicuous clothes gather in a group, their presence alone makes them difficult to approach. Everyone averts their eyes and gives them space, and I suppose that steadily emboldened them—”

lines.japanese: 「──いまや彼らは、一端のアウトロー気取りですよ。まだ表沙汰になるほどではないみたいですけど、ちらほら他のグループと小競り合いを起こしてるような話は聞きますね」
lines.english: “—until now they fancy themselves full-fledged outlaws. It hasn’t spilled out into the open yet, but I hear the occasional story about them getting into skirmishes with other groups.”

lines.japanese: 他のグループ……っていうと、鳳ンとこのああいう連中のことか？
lines.english: Other groups... Did he mean people like Otori's crowd?

lines.japanese: ああ、そうか、さらに繋がった。
lines.english: Ah. Right. Another connection.

lines.japanese: 前に森里が言ってた自称“聖戦”の抗争相手「キモくてヤバい連中」ってのも、そういやＲなんたらだ。
lines.english: The ‘creepy, dangerous freaks’ Morisato once said they were fighting in their self-proclaimed holy war—that had been R-something too.

lines.japanese: 激突！　悪の帝国フレイムバーズＶＳ暗黒教団Ｒ－ウィング！
lines.english: Clash! The Evil Flame Birds Empire versus the Dark R-Wing Order!

lines.japanese: どうでもいい。超どうでもいい。
lines.english: I didn't care. I really didn't care.

lines.japanese: 「ったくよー、クサクサしてんだか何だか知んねーけど、善良な一般市民に八つ当たりすんなっつーの」
lines.english: “Whatever's eating them, they need to quit taking it out on innocent civilians.”

lines.japanese: 「はい？　なんです？」
lines.english: “Hmm? What was that?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、さっき俺、まさにそのＲなんたらいう馬鹿共に、目が合った何だってしつけーイチャモン付けられたばっかだわ」
lines.english: “I just had those R-whatever idiots hounding me because I made eye contact with them.”

lines.japanese: 「本当ですか？　ええ、それはまた……ドラさん相手に命知らずな……」
lines.english: “Really? My... They must have a death wish, picking a fight with you.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、実際ンとこ、俺がこんな心の広い人間じゃなかったら、あいつら三回ぐらい死んでたろうな」
lines.english: “Yeah. If I weren't such an extraordinarily broad-minded man, they'd probably have died three times over.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラさんのは心が広いと言うより、心が鈍いって感じですけどね」
lines.english: “I’d call that a numb heart, not a big one, Dora.”

lines.japanese: 「おお、なるほど」
lines.english: “Oh. Fair point.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせーよ。なるほどじゃねーよ。さりげに他人の本質見透かしてんじゃねーよ、ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Shut up. What do you mean, ‘fair point’? Don’t go casually seeing right through me. I’ll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「あれっ、単なる冗談だったんですけど、当たってました？」
lines.english: “Oh? It was only a joke. Did I hit the mark?”

lines.japanese: 「知らねえよ。俺を見透かしてる暇あったら、女の服でも見透かしてろ。だっちーの胸でも見透かしてろ」
lines.english: “Hell if I know. If you've got time to see through me, use your X-ray vision on women's clothes. Use it on Datchi's chest.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、足立アナの……たしかにあの噂はセンセーショナルでした。ショックというよりほかありません」
lines.english: “Ah, announcer Adachi's... That rumor certainly was sensational. Shocking is the only word.”

lines.japanese: 「まーなァ、分かるけどな。硬派で知られる俺でさえ、あいつの胸についムラッと来たのは一回や二回じゃねーよ」
lines.english: “Yeah, I get it. Even a hard-boiled guy like me has felt the old animal stir over that chest more than once or twice.”

lines.japanese: 「いえ、僕はべつに、彼女の補正疑惑が事実だったとしても、それはいいんです。だって女性が自らを飾りたてる行為は、周囲への気配りとも言えるわけでしょう。それはとても素敵なことだと思うんです」
lines.english: “No, if the rumors about padding are true, I don't mind. A woman's efforts to make herself beautiful can be called consideration for those around her, can't they? I think that's a wonderful thing.”

lines.japanese: 「ただ……あの噂を耳にするまで、何の疑念も抱かなかった自分の未熟さに……くっ」
lines.english: “It's only... what hurts is my own immaturity—not suspecting a thing until I heard the rumor... Ngh.”

lines.japanese: 「だァいじょぶだって元気出せよ、まだウソ胸だって決まったわけじゃねンだから。な、俺たちはこれからも、やつの胸を信じて見守ってきゃあいーじゃん」
lines.english: “It's all right. Cheer up. Nobody's proven they're fake yet. We can keep believing in them and watching over them together.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、でもドラさんは小さい胸の方がお好みなんですよね」
lines.english: “Oh? But Dora, I thought you preferred smaller breasts.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、女豹」
lines.english: “No. Panthers.”

lines.japanese: 「ふむ、いわゆるロリ巨乳という？」
lines.english: “Hmm. The underage-but-busty type, as they say?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、頭のカタカナ二文字はべつに」
lines.english: “No. I could do without the ‘underage’ part.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、普通の子でも大丈夫ってことじゃないですか！　なんだ、だったらまだ更正できますよ。そうだ、実は最近、四個前の元カノが会うたびイイ男を紹介しろってうるさかったんです。彼女は昆虫……あ、ドラさん」
lines.english: “What? Then an ordinary girl would be fine! In that case, there's hope for your rehabilitation yet. Actually, the girlfriend from four relationships ago has started demanding I introduce her to a good man every time we meet. She's an insect… Oh, Dora.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: ツッコミ所が多くなってきたので勝手に喋らせていたら、急に呼びとめられた。振りむくとやつは、親指を分岐路の一方に向けていた。
lines.english: There was so much wrong with that I didn’t know where to start, so I let him ramble. Then he suddenly stopped me. I turned to find him pointing his thumb down one fork in the road.

lines.japanese: 「すみません、僕こっちなんで。ここで失礼します」
lines.english: “Sorry, I’m going this way. This is where we part.”

lines.japanese: 「あー。あーそう。んーじゃ」
lines.english: “Oh. Right. Well, then.”

lines.japanese: 「はい、お疲れさまです」
lines.english: “Have a good shift.”

lines.japanese: またなとは言わず、中途半端な会話をまとめることもなく、俺たちはその場であっさり別れた。
lines.english: Just like that, we went our separate ways—no see you, no attempt to tie off the conversation we had left hanging.

lines.japanese: 次の約束はない。互いのアドレスも電話番号も本名さえも知らない。偶然の遭遇がなければ、これが今生の別れとなるのかもしれない。しれないけど、でもたぶん、この辺りをうろついてればきっとまた会える。
lines.english: There was no next appointment. We didn't know each other's email addresses, phone numbers, or even real names. Unless chance brought us together, this might be our final farewell in this life. It might—but if we kept wandering around this neighborhood, we would probably meet again.

lines.japanese: そういうあやふやな繋がり方が、あやふやな存在の俺には気楽だった。
lines.english: That kind of tenuous connection suited a tenuous existence like mine.

lines.japanese: 突きつめて言えばプラチナだってそうなんだろう。やつがひとりのパートナーと長続きしないのは、繋がりが太くなることに煩雑さを覚えるから。絆が強くなることに魅力を感じないからだ。
lines.english: Follow the thought through and Platinum was probably the same. He never stayed with one partner for long because he found close ties troublesome. Stronger bonds held no appeal for him.

lines.japanese: いつだったか、いつもの屋台でいつもの常連たちとラーメンを食ってたとき、ほどよく酔ったプラチナが砕けた敬語で俺に聞いてきた。なんでドラさん彼女作んないんすかあ。
lines.english: Once, over ramen with the usual regulars at the usual stall, a pleasantly drunk Platinum had asked me, his usual polite speech gone loose at the seams: *How come you never get yourself a girlfriend, Dora?*

lines.japanese: そういう給湯室のＯＬみたいな会話を好かない俺が顔をしかめていると、ちんぴらエージが横から勝手に答えた。ムリムリ、ドラは女に声かけたり口説いたりってのド下手だもん。
lines.english: I hated that sort of office-break-room relationship gossip and pulled a face. The hoodlum Eiji answered for me: *No chance. Dora’s absolute shit at approaching women or sweet-talking them.*

lines.japanese: そしたら今度はパルさんが割って入る。そんなもんおまえ、なまじっか上手かったらプラチナみたいな遊び人になっちまわあ。
lines.english: Paru cut in next: *Hell, if he were even halfway good at that stuff, he’d wind up a playboy like Platinum.*

lines.japanese: するとプラチナはこともなげにこう返す。やだなあパルさん、遊び人ってのは必ずしも口説くのが上手いわけじゃないんすよー？
lines.english: Platinum answered as though it were nothing: *Come now, Paru. Being a playboy doesn’t necessarily mean you’re any good at winning women over.*

lines.japanese: ああん、じゃあ何が上手いってんだい。パルさんが問いただすと、やつはにっこり笑ってこう答えた。
lines.english: *Oh? Then what are you good at?* Paru demanded. He smiled brightly and answered.

lines.japanese: 別れるのが、上手いんです。
lines.english: *Breaking up with them.*

lines.japanese: おあとがよろしいようで。ぺこり。
lines.english: And on that note, thank you and good night. *Bow.*
